title: Eleven Productions and One Empty Stage
subtitle: 戏剧与表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧与表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧与表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：director　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 director 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 the company ① engaged a director that no theatre in the city would have trusted, and they said the engaging was the whole of the season. The ② director, meaning the person and not the post, ran eleven productions and stayed unnamed on the poster; a director, they said, is the only thing in a company that is judged by how long he is left uncredited.

Every ③ director in that company had the same empty stage at the end of the rehearsal, and the ④ director at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A director, the stage manager said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to watch; the company said the watching is the part that fills eleven productions.

The accountant meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the director was the whole of the board, meaning the post and not the person. The ⑥ director, meaning the post and not any of that, is the only thing on a board that everybody votes for and nobody fills; director, he said, is either somebody you engage or the only word that means both a person and a post. He said the post is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ director had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the empty stage. The ⑧ director of the whole thing, the company wrote in April, was one season and eleven productions of watching; director, they said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to watch. She said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ director I remember is the one at the end, who retired in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the city. A ⑩ director, the stage manager said in 1970, is the only one who improves by being thanked; every director, she said, is a post that has agreed to look like a person. She said the post was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 导演（指剧团聘请的那一位）
B. n. 导演（指那个人本身，与那个职位相对）
C. 固定搭配：engage a director 聘请一位导演
D. n. 导演（指留给最后一部戏用的那一位）
E. n. 导演；执导（抽象总称，指一个剧团的导演之职）
F. n. 导演（指节目单上写到、被列名的那一位）
G. n. 董事；理事职位（指董事会里被选举的席位）
H. n. 董事席位（抽象总称，指人人投票却无人担任的席位）

items.q: engaged a director that no theatre in the city would have trusted
The director, meaning the person and not the post
the director was the whole of the board
the director had become a line in a programme
The director of the whole thing
A director, the stage manager said in 1970

answers.why: engage a director 意为“聘请一位导演”，1946 年剧团聘请了一位全城没有一家剧院肯信任的导演。
director 意为“导演”，指那个人本身而不是那个职位，他执导了十一部戏而在海报上没有署名。
director 意为“导演”，指那个剧团里每一位导演，每一次排练末尾都是同一个空舞台。
director 意为“导演”，指留给最后一部戏用的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
director 意为“董事、理事职位”，指董事会里被选举的席位，会计说这个席位就是那届董事会的全部。
director 意为“董事席位”，指人人投票却无人担任的席位而不是那个人本身，是董事会里人人都投票、却无人担任的席位。
director 意为“导演”，指节目单上写到、被列名的那一位，到 1955 年这位导演成了节目单里的一行。
director 意为“导演、执导”，剧团四月写道，整件事的执导是一个演出季和十一部戏的审视。
director 意为“导演”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1968 年退休，至今仍被说成全城最安静的一位。
director 为抽象总称，舞台监督 1970 年说，一位导演是唯一会因为被致谢而变得更好的人。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1946 年剧团聘请了一位全城没有一家剧院肯信任的导演，他们说聘请才是这个演出季的全部。（engage a director）
那位导演，指的是那个人本身而不是那个职位，执导了十一部戏而在海报上没有署名。（director）
那个剧团里每一位导演的排练末尾都是同一个空舞台。（director）
末尾那一位导演，指的是他们留给最后一部戏用的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（director）
会计说这个席位就是那届董事会的全部，指的是那个董事职位而不是那个人。（director）
1970 年舞台监督说，一位导演是唯一会因为被致谢而变得更好的人。（director）

Every director in that company had the same empty stage at the end of the rehearsal.
The director at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
The accountant said the director was the whole of the board, meaning the post and not the person.
